description.narrative: Improving transboundary collaboration, supporting effective management, providing relevant accessible information, and promoting inclusive development

Number of regional and international collaborative engagements. For year 2022, Several conservation events were attended, with GVTC active participation, organization of side events, distribution of information materials etc. In this respects, especially GVTC officials have participated in the African Parc Congress which took place in Kigali July 2022. They have attended also the CITES conference in Panama, and CBD conference in Montreal Canada. GVTC officials have attended the Congo Bassin Forest Partnership conference in Libreville Gabon. GVTC Secretariat has presented in the Ecosystem Services partnership Africa Conference held in Classic Hotel, Musanze, Rwanda on 8th to 10th June 2022. The outcome of these meetings were to raise awareness of GVTC and the GVL but also to boost the networking for a potential fundraising for GVTC financial sustainability. On the sideline of CDB, GVTC officials have recognized the role of the youth in GVL conservation and have recognized to the youth who are in the Global Youth Biodiversity Network the chapiter of Rwanda, Uganda and DRC. They will be since then, members of the GVTC stakeholders forum. During the CBD Conference, Dr. Andrew G. Seguya, GVTC Executive Secretary has spoken on Science and traditional knowledge as a requirement for ecosystems restoration side events. The visibility of GVTC is much greater.

Measurable indicator: Number of wildlife crime cases reported / handled by agencies in TB wildlife crime prevention; and Number of coordinated patrols conducted in transboundary wildlife crime hotspot areas. Description and unit of measurement and disaggregation: Count of wildlife crime cases handled and Count of coordinated patrols. As a result, due to Covid-19, coordinated patrols were not conducted in transboundary wildlife crime crime hotspot areas.
For year 2022, Consultations made with the relevant institutions on the security related issues for wildlife; GVTC played a key role in solving the issue of transboundary Human wildlife conflict in Bugeshi, where an electrical fence was broken, allowing the passage of park wild animals from the PNVi (DRC) into the field of the communities on the side of Rwanda. This issue was solved through the rehabilitation of the electrical fence and reinstallation of electricity into the fence. However prevailing security conditions, it was not possible to organise the meeting.

Treaty ratified. Treaty ratification critical steps in each partner state identified. Consultations done with Ministers in All PS. Uganda drafted a paper for the cabinet.
In 2022, GVTC has held briefing sessions with the Ministers in Uganda and Rwanda; GVTC contributed to the drafting of the Cabinet paper for GVTC treaty ratification. In Uganda the process is at an advance stage. In Rwanda, the cabinet paper was prepared but at the Cabinet meeting of Rwanda, the Government of Rwanda has suggested that the Summit be removed from the GVTC Governing structure, the Board has approved this move, and this is on the agenda of the forthcoming GVTC Council of Ministers.
